title: herbstutil
description: the herbstluftwm compatibility layer: herbstclient attr output as clean typed JSON, shell completion mirroring herbstclient's own, and the parse/attr primitives every sibling tool builds on.

content.heading: herbstutil - the JSON bridge to herbstluftwm
content: **herbstutil** is a small command-line tool that turns the output of `herbstclient attr` into clean, typed JSON - so the state of the **herbstluftwm** window manager can be consumed wherever JSON is spoken.
it can run herbstclient itself (`herbstutil attr ...`) or parse piped output like a unix filter.
[https://github.com/akinevz2/herbstutil](https://github.com/akinevz2/herbstutil)

content.heading: the attr interface herbstclient speaks
content: **herbstluftwm** is a manual tiling window manager for Linux. its core idea: the whole desktop is one global object tree - monitors, tags, clients (windows), settings - queried and modified over IPC with the companion tool herbstclient.
the tree is probed with `herbstclient attr <path>`: it prints a short description of the node, its children, and a table of every attribute (typed, writable, hookable).

```sh
$ herbstclient attr clients.            # children of the clients node
$ herbstclient attr clients.focus.      # introspect the focused window
$ herbstclient attr clients.focus.tag   # read a single leaf value
```
the catch: `attr` output is written for humans first - padded type tables, prose, legends.
great to read, fragile to parse.

content.heading: the package, architecturally
content: one **bun**/**bunli** single executable: a pure parse/attr core, exported as a library (parseAttr), under a thin command layer - `attr`, `parse`, `shell-completions`.
every spawn of herbstclient and helper binaries carries the 5-second timeout the dots wrapper convention mandates: a vanished window resolves null instead of wedging the bar or the keybind.
parse/attr primitives only - the keybind state machines live one floor down, in **herbctl**.

content.heading: usage
content: two ways to the same JSON: let herbstutil run herbstclient for you, or pipe herbstclient through the parse filter (the default command):

```sh
$ herbstutil attr clients.focus.           # runs herbstclient attr and parses it
$ herbstclient attr clients. | herbstutil parse
$ herbstclient attr clients. | herbstutil   # parse is the default command
```
`-s, --space <n>` - pretty-print with `n` spaces of indentation (default 4)
`-e, --escape` - skip all type conversion and keep every value exactly as herbstclient printed it: strings keep their literal quotes, escaped inside the JSON string
`parse` refuses to run attached to a terminal: as a filter it always reads from stdin.

content.heading: quirks - the value typing
content: herbstclient annotates every attribute with a type hint in the first column of its listing; herbstutil uses that hint to emit properly typed JSON:
`s` (string) - JSON string, outer quotes stripped
`b` (bool) - JSON boolean
`i`, `u` (int, uint) - JSON number
`R` (rectangle) - `WIDTHxHEIGHT+X+Y` becomes an object { x, y, width, height }
`p` (point) - `XxY` becomes an object { x, y }
`c`, `r`, `n`, `f` (color, regex, named value, font) - string
leaf values (a single attribute) print no type hint, so a heuristic decides there: true/false become booleans, integers and decimals become numbers, everything else stays a string.
pass `--escape` to keep the raw text instead.

content.heading: stable in v1.x
content: the global command installs from a plain `npm install -g herbstutil` wherever bun exists - the package runs its bun-executed source, no build step to trust and no dist blob to ship.
the help text is terse and prints on stdout; the version in bunli.config and package.json can never diverge (the config spreads the package manifest).
the completion verb ships as `shell-completions`, registered first so help reads attr, parse, shell-completions in the natural order.
the parse contract is the stable surface: typed JSON with value / children / attributes, rectangles and points as objects.

content.heading: extensions - shell completion
content: **herbstclient**'s completion model: the binary does the thinking (complete_shell <pos> <words...>), the shell scripts just delegate. **herbstutil** mirrors it - the shell-completions verb, plus bash/zsh scripts that are byte-structure twins of hlwm's own.

the attr verb's positional completes live hlwm object paths: the request is delegated to herbstclient -q complete_shell itself, so clients.0x…, tags.by-name. and every attribute name arrive straight from the running WM.
install the completion with the package scripts:

```sh
$ npm run completion:install     # bash + zsh, user-level
$ herbstutil attr clients.<TAB>  # the live tree, in your shell
```
published on npm: `npm i -g herbstutil` gives the command (it runs through bun) - or install from source with `bun run build`.
